WoW: Forever

Retribution Paladin

Two-handed melee with Holy magic layered on top. Holy Strike at level 6 — twenty levels earlier than Classic gave a Paladin a button — turns it from auto-attack-and-wait into something you actually play.

WoW: Forever · Melee DPS · Updated October 5, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70124 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Retribution build has been tested. A specific warning for this spec: a widely-published level-30 Retribution build spends two points on Crusade, a talent that does not exist in the beta client, it vanished from the Retribution tree in the September 24 build (1.60.1.70009), the beta's first balance pass, with no mention in Blizzard's notes. That build cannot be entered as printed, and no source publishes a legal replacement. Separately, Wowhead reports that beta testers and class discords currently consider Retribution the single most overtuned spec in the level-20 bracket, with changes expected — the level-30 cap opened on October 1, and that same build cut Champion of the Light — so treat the talent and gearing advice below as a snapshot, not a settled answer.

What Retribution is for

Layering Holy damage onto a two-handed swing, with a real button to press from level 6. Holy Strike arrives at 6, twenty levels before Classic gave a Paladin one, and Sacred Arbiter later makes it refresh all Judgement debuffs, so staying in melee maintains them without re-judging. Seal of Command at 20 procs Holy damage scaled off the swing, and leading with Hammer of Justice makes its Judgement hit far harder into a stunned target.

What the sources say about levelling in it, and the one that speaks to this spec directly is emphatic: Wowhead reports that beta testers and class discords currently consider Retribution the single most overtuned spec in the level-20 bracket, with changes expected. That is not a levelling score — no source publishes one for any Paladin spec, and a score would rate solo kill speed anyway.

Two honest caveats. You have no area damage whatsoever until Consecration at 20, so do not pull more than you can kill one at a time. And Paladin has no movement tools at all, it is described as "slow, very slow."

One tip that generalises: treat mana as an extension of your health bar. Topping yourself up with Holy Light and killing the next thing at low mana usually beats sitting down to drink.

Your talent points

Level 20: 0/0/11.

  1. Deflection, 5 points — +5% parry, and Forever moved it to tier 1 so it is available from level 10
  2. Improved Judgement, 2 points
  3. Conviction, 3 points, this is forced, not a preference: Seal of Command is a tier-3 talent needing 10 points in the tree, and 5+2+1 would not reach it
  4. Seal of Command at 20

The published respec at 20, for mana rather than damage: Benediction 5, Holy Conduit 2, Improved Judgement 2, Conviction 1, Seal of Command 1. It makes Consecration affordable and cheapens Exorcism, which matters in Ruins of Lordaeron and Shadowfang Keep.

A second published build drops Improved Judgement for two more Conviction, on the grounds that "mana is simply not an issue at level 20 with the new changes." Both are defensible.

Wowhead goes further and questions the whole premise. Its testers find Seal of Command not meaningfully better than Seal of Righteousness at 20 once you account for talents and spell power, and currently rate a Holy-leaning "Shockadin" build, the final point going to Divine Intellect, Voice of Truth or mana regen instead, then aiming at Holy Shock and Champion of the Light later, as the stronger PvE choice right now, against this page's "Seal Twist" build, which Wowhead rates weaker in PvE at 20 but ahead in PvP burst with a slow two-hander.

Rotation

  1. Always have a seal up: Seal of Righteousness, or Seal of Command once talented
  2. On anything that will survive several Judgements, judge Seal of the Crusader first for the Holy damage amplifier, then switch back. This is cheap now: Judgement no longer consumes the seal, and the debuff lasts 40 seconds
  3. Holy Strike on cooldown, as mana allows
  4. Judgement on cooldown, as mana allows
  5. With Seal of Command, Hammer of Justice first — Judgement of Command hits far harder into a stunned target
  6. Exorcism against Undead and Demons only
  7. Maintain a Blessing and an Aura; top up with Holy Light

Multi-target: none until 20. Then Consecration, and it is expensive. Blizzard publishes no target cap for it: the patchy damage beyond the first few targets was a bug, and the September 24 build fixed Consecration's failure to apply its increased damage effect to some targets, along with its inconsistent Z axis.

Later, Sacred Arbiter gives Holy Strike +20% damage — raised from 10% in the September 24 build — and makes it refresh all Judgement debuffs, so staying in melee maintains them without re-judging.

Stat priority

Weapon DPS, then Hit and Expertise, critical strike, Spell Power, Strength, Intellect, Agility, Stamina.

Hit and Expertise barely appear on gear at this level, so they are close to irrelevant below 30. A slower weapon makes Holy Strike hit harder, but raw weapon DPS usually wins. Intellect jumps sharply at 26 points in the tree, level 35, where Champion of the Light starts converting it into spell damage, up to 60% of it at the talent's max rank, 20% per point spent — cut from 33% per point (100% at max) in the October 1 build, so expect Wowhead, Icy Veins and ClassicWoW.gg to still carry the old number until they update. Blizzard also removed a tooltip line that claimed the talent increased Healing too; it never did, so treat this as spell damage only.

Published gear lists split into a Spell Power build and an Attack Power build and call both competitive at level 20.

What defines Retribution

Talent or abilityEarliest levelWhat it does
Holy Strike6, baseline25% of weapon damage at the rank you train at 6, rising per rank to 50% at rank 8, plus a flat Holy component. 10-second cooldown, lowered from 12 in the September 24 build, which also flattened the curve to 25/29/32/36/39/43/46/50% (was 25/25/30/30/35/35/40/40%) because "early ranks of Holy Strike didn't always feel like an upgrade", and removed Improved Holy Strike from the tree. Only the added component is Holy — armour still reduces the weapon half
Seal of Commandexactly 20Procs Holy damage scaled off the swing, so it wants a slow two-hander. Its Judgement is amplified against stunned targets
Benediction + Holy Conduit10 and 15The mana economy, and the reason the level-20 respec exists

What Forever changed for Retribution

  • Six new talents: Holy Conduit, Sanctified Judgement, Sacred Arbiter, Champion of the Light, Instrument of Law, and the Twist of Light capstone.
  • Four talents deleted: Improved Blessing of Might, Improved Retribution Aura, Improved Seal of the Crusader, Sanctity Aura.
  • Crusade is gone from the Retribution tree, removed in the September 24 build with no note from Blizzard.
  • Vindication now also grants you attack power. Vengeance moved a tier and now stacks, up to 3 times rather than Classic's single 8-second buff — the September 24 build lowered the maximum from 5, and in the same build made it activate off non-periodic critical strikes only, closing a Known Issue where periodic crits fed it. Eye for an Eye reflect cut from 30% to 10%. Pursuit of Justice now covers mounted speed. Two-Handed Weapon Specialization is 2% per rank, 6% at max, cut from 3/6/9% in the September 24 build; Icy Veins and ClassicWoW.gg still carry the old 3% in their talent data.

At level 60

Unknown. Whether the Twist of Light capstone or a Holy hybrid wins is an untested either-or at 51 points, and the author of one published guide now says "it's looking like twisting might not be the way to go for Paladin raid DPS specs atm."

Compiled from the three major Forever guide sites and cross-checked against each other. Everything else — talent ranks, tooltip values, what exists in the tree at all — is settled against the client itself, read through foreverchanges.pro and wago.tools.
